To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a smartphone app to track and report energy use is effective in increasing energy awareness; and (2) a smartphone app is effective in changing behavior, but the effect is short-term and requires repeated use.
(a) people are willing to engage in sustainable behaviors and that (b) they are willing to engage with technology that supports those behaviors.

(i) the use of the word “sustainability” in HCI research has increased significantly since the publication of Blevis’ seminal paper, and that (ii) the use of this word in HCI research has been associated with a significant increase in the number of citations to the paper.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people can work together to address sustainability issues.
the design of interactive systems and services to support sustainability, and with the development of theoretical and methodological approaches to the design of such systems and services.
the ways in which people interact with and experience their everyday environment, including the ways in which their actions and experiences shape and are shaped by the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no conclusive statements.
the problem of sustainability is a wicked one, which cannot be solved by any single approach, but rather by a combination of many approaches.
there is a need for more work that addresses the systemic nature of sustainability and the social and cultural dimensions of the problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is not enough to focus only on the user, but that we must consider how the user is embedded in larger systems.
it is important to consider the social, economic, and political factors that constrain and enable individuals’ actions.
we are trying to move the discipline of HCI beyond the focus on individual users and to develop methods and theories that can address the social and environmental problems that we face.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a range of different ways in which HCI can contribute to sustainability, and that we need to be open to new approaches and new ways of thinking about the problems we face.
there is an urgent need to understand how to work at different scales, including the scale of the community, the organization, or even the city.
we need to move beyond a narrow focus on the individual to understand how to intervene at the group, organizational and community levels.
